subject.title: Feature: Per-spawn tool restrictions for sub-agents

question: Should OpenClaw accept the active PR's allowlist-first `sessions_spawn.toolsAllow` API as the first per-spawn restriction contract, or require a broader allow/deny/no-tools policy before landing?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the chosen public API controls a security boundary and durable spawned-session behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Accept allowlist-first V1
options.body: Land or polish the current `toolsAllow` candidate as an additive first contract, with explicit docs for empty lists and unsupported runtimes.

options.title: Require broader policy shape
options.body: Hold the candidate until the public API directly covers allow, deny, and no-tools semantics described across the related issues.

options.title: Defer unified policy design
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers design one model for spawned sessions, route bindings, delegated tools, and plugin/MCP resolution.

recommendation.title: Accept allowlist-first V1
recommendation.body: Land or polish the current `toolsAllow` candidate as an additive first contract, with explicit docs for empty lists and unsupported runtimes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available prior-review and current maintainer-decision routing signal for this API/security boundary.
